The heavy lane runs one job at a time in order of priority (1 a person's request, 2 an agent's, the default, 3 sweeps and batches; a waiting job rises one level after a minute), then in turns between owners, then in order of submission. The job carries a frozen copy of the project: later edits do not change it (`project_changed` says they happened). `supersede` replaces a queued request of the same kind and targets; `hold` keeps it from starting until `queue_release`. description: Queues one solve per point and returns the sweep's number at once. A point is a list of edits (`{ "cmd": "set_param", "args": { "name": "w", "value": 4e-7 } }`: any command that changes the project except those that replace it or start work), applied to a copy of the project: what varies, a geometry parameter, the wavelength in the study, a material, a mesh setting, is the case's to decide. Give `points` (each `{ label, edits }`) or `series` (`{ cmd, args, field, values }`: the command repeated with `field` set to each value). `physics` is the code or list solved at every point (default: what a solve would solve). The points are queued at priority 3 (sweeps and batches) so a person's request and a single request of an agent go before them, and run on the same mesh and solve caches as any request. Every point's edits are applied and checked first: a bad point fails the request with its number and nothing runs. The project, the mesh and the results of the engine are not touched; each point is recorded in the run table when the project is bound to a workflow. Read the table with `sweep_table`.

description: A handle to a field of a solution, to compute with (`integrate`, `extremum`, `probe`, `line_cut`, `overlap`, `confinement`, `field_op`). A handle is a small value, not the field: it names the physics, the solution and the field, and is read from the stored result each time it is used. A name is a per-cell field of the solution (`Ex`, `uz`, ...: complex when the solve is) or else a flat field of `result_info` (`T`, `|E|`: real). A vector name (`E` when `Ex` and `Ez` exist) answers one handle per component.

title: Arithmetic on handles

description: The integral of an expression of fields over a region (a region name, comma list or `name*`; default the whole mesh), with the degree-4 rule of the finite elements (exact for the product of two P2 fields). A real expression answers a number, a complex one [re, im]. `measure` is the area or volume of the region. `revolution: true` weights by 2 pi r for a body of revolution (a 2D r-z mesh). BATCH REDUCTIONS: pass `solutions` (`"all"` or a list of 0-based indices), `by_region: true`, or a batch `expr` list `["abs2(Ex)", "abs2(Ey)"]` / named map `{"energy": "...", "ex2": "..."}` to evaluate every `(solution, region, expr)` combination in a single bit-exact quadrature pass. Answers `stale` and `age_s` of what it read. FORMULAS (every `expr` of the reductions takes one): a text such as `abs(Ex)^2 * eps_r` or `where(x > 0, T, 0)`, parsed once and evaluated at each point in Rust. Numbers (`2j` is imaginary), `pi`, `e`, `+ - * / ^`, comparisons, `and or not`; functions `abs abs2 re im conj sqrt exp sin cos arg log log10 tan sinh cosh tanh atan step min max atan2` and `where(cond, a, b)` (only the branch that applies is evaluated, so `where(x != 0, 1/x, 0)` is safe). Names: the coordinates `x y z`; the fields of the result (`Ex`, `T`; in backticks when the name is not an identifier, `` `|E|` ``; `` `ems:Ex` `` or `` `ems:1:Ex` `` in backticks for another physics or solution); material values by their descriptor name (`eps_r`, `rho`; `eps` means `eps_r`; `material("rho")` to be explicit); `region("Si")` is 1 inside the region and 0 outside. A name like `E` stands for the vector (Ex, Ey, Ez) when the solution has those components: `dot(a, b)`, `inner(a, b)` (conjugates a), `cross`, `norm(v)`, `norm2(v)`, `E.x`. Orders, comparisons, `log` and `tan` read real values: wrap a complex one in `abs`, `re` or `im`. A material value is the one the solver saw in each cell. A tensor property (`eps_r`, `k`, `alpha`) has its entries as `eps_r_xx`, `eps_r_yy`, `eps_r_zz`, `eps_r_xy`, `eps_r_xz`, `eps_r_yz` in wafer axes with the crystal orientation applied (an isotropic material is the scalar times the identity); the plain `eps_r` is refused on a mesh where some material is a tensor. BOUNDARY INTEGRALS: with `boundary` (an outer boundary such as "window.top", an interface "oxide|silicon", or an interior 3D sheet) the sum is over the facets of the boundary instead of the cells: a line integral on a 2D mesh, a surface integral on a 3D one, with `revolution` weighting by 2 pi r. The formula may use `nx`, `ny`, `nz`, the unit normal in wafer axes, so the flux of a vector F is `dot(F, [nx, ny, nz])`. At an interface or interior sheet give `side` (a region name, or "+z"/"-z" for a sheet inside one region); the normal points out of it. On an outer boundary no `side` is needed. `wavelength` (m) reads the material values at that wavelength, not the study's; the fields stay those of the solve.

description: Solves the physics on a second mesh with element sizes multiplied by `factor` (`< 1` refines, `> 1` coarsens; the active project is never mutated) and compares every eigenvalue, value and scalar between the coarse and fine grids. By default `scale_sizes` is true so non-suppressed `add_size` rules (`h`, `max_deviation`, `min_layers`) and `gap_cells` scale proportionally with `factor` on the comparison copy. With `tolerance` each row says pass or fail, `converged` summarises, and the verdict is kept (`validated` becomes `checked` or stays `exploratory`). When mode ordering changes between meshes, `match: "nearest"` pairs mutual nearest eigenvalues and `track` filters candidate modes on both meshes by target (`f`, `n_b` or `n_eff`) and/or physical mode signatures (`region`/`min_share`, `component`/`min_component`, `max_layer_fraction`). With `extrapolate` (`"richardson_log_spd"` or `"richardson_linear"`), computes two-grid Richardson extrapolation (`extrapolate_order` defaults to 1.0 on 3D/sheet capacitance matrices, else `2 * order`) and optionally promotes the extrapolated capacitance matrix onto the stored result when `apply_extrapolated` is true.
name: convergence_check

extrapolate_order.description: asymptotic convergence order p > 0 for Richardson extrapolation; default 1.0 for 3D/sheet capacitance matrices, else 2 * order

factor.description: comparison/present element-size ratio, positive and not 1 (< 1 refines, > 1 coarsens), default 0.6

match.description: how the solutions of the two meshes are paired: index (default) compares solution i with solution i; nearest pairs each mode with the nearest eigenvalue of the other mesh in the complex plane and lists the modes without a partner

max_cells.description: refuse, before any solve, a check whose comparison mesh has more cells than this (an adaptive 2D mesh has 6 to 8 times as many cells at factor 0.6)

description: Runs an analysis on the latest result of a physics: polarization, capacitance_matrix, inductance_matrix, epr, hamiltonian, tls_participation, or network. For `capacitance_matrix`, optional `params` perform ground projection or floating Schur elimination (`ground`, `eliminate: "drop" | "floating_schur"`), grounded/differential lumped qubit reduction (`qubits: [{ name, pads, E_J_Hz? }]`), resonator ZPF / dispersive coupling extraction (`resonators: [{ name, terminal, f_r_Hz, Z0_ohm?, resonator_type?, C_r_F? }]`), and matched-asymptotic finite-metal-thickness correction (`metal_thickness_m`, `edge_cutoff_m`). For `hamiltonian`, outputs include `f_cav_Hz`, `g_matrix_Hz`, `kappa_cav_Hz`, and `t1_purcell_s`, and `params` accept `sweep_port` (0-based index or port name), `squid_asymmetry`, `squid_flux_sweep`, and `ej_hz_sweep`. For `tls_participation`, interface thicknesses/permittivities/loss tangents auto-load from the material TOML `[interfaces.{ma,ms,sa}]` and `params` accept `trench_depth_m` (substrate over-etch depth in metres). For `network`, extracts damped companion-QEP modes, ROM-synthesized Z/Y/S matrices, Schur-complement Black-Box Quantization (`bbq_modes`), Taubin algebraic circle-fit resonator parameters (`s21_fit`), and Touchstone v1.1 (`.sNp`) text from either `CircuitRom` or `DrivenPortData`. The reply carries `stale`, `age_s`, and `validated` of the result it was run on.
name: analyse

params.description: optional analysis parameters (capacitance_matrix: ground, eliminate, qubits, resonators, metal_thickness_m, edge_cutoff_m; hamiltonian: basis, fock_trunc, sweep_port, flux_sweep, squid_asymmetry, squid_flux_sweep, ej_hz_sweep; tls_participation: trench_depth_m, t_ma/t_ms/t_sa, etc.; network: freqs_hz, terminations_ohm, active_ports, s21_ports, resonator_branch, touchstone_format; epr options)
